mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the 60-day forward window, leading to negative 60-day SPX returns despite accelerating GDP.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) over a 3-month period signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input constraints and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 55% of instances following a 3-month INDPRO drop > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 2-month period signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns are positive in > 40% of instances following a 2-month UNRATE rise > 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positive in > 45% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both decline by more than 5% over a 6-month period, it signals a broad-based weakening of consumer demand that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day SPX returns are positive in > 40% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 5% over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) rises by more than 3% over a 6-month period and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals a supply-constrained environment that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from pricing power.
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are negative in > 40% of instances when INDPRO rises > 3% over 6 months and UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 3% over a 12-month period and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, it signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as companies pass on higher costs to consumers.
failure_condition: 60-day SPX returns are negative in > 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 3% over 12 months and FEDFUNDS < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises by more than 200,000 over a 3-month period, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending remains robust.
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong job growth
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are negative in > 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS rises > 200,000 over 3 months.
